extra.description: extra.state: tab_groups, saved_tab_groups, workspace_groups, workspace_placements, rooms, screen_groups, closed, workspace_status, workspace_checklist, window_records, sidebar_layout, sidebar. Open: x-oracle-id-patterns and x-oracle-open-keys apply

x-oracle-volatile.reason: settings.snapshot write counter; counts writes, not state

file_sha256.description: the parsed user file (effective.file_root), canonical JSON

domains.description: value domains the app published; null for one never published

oracle.description: oracle-state extras (oracle cargo feature or debug build only)

liveObjects.description: object kind to live count, sorted keys

focus.description: Focus model next to AppKit, Ghostty and layout focus, per window.

responder.description: the classified first responder's kind; its pane is responderPane

responderPane.description: the pane the first responder is in; null for a responder outside every pane

childPage.description: the tab whose Chromium page window has focus; a cmux page's Chromium tab id is mapped to its tab key, so it differs from debug.focus child_window_page (raw page id) for a cmux page

x-oracle-source.from: FocusApplier.focusedChildWindowPageID mapped to the tab key

x-oracle-volatile.reason: FocusCoordinator bump count; counts focus passes, not state

consistent.description: no InputInvariants.world violation names this window. Not debug.focus's consistent (layout, W1 and Ghostty only): F, W4, W5, W6 (sheet), W7 and W8 violations count here too. An unsettled window is not inconsistent (settle is debug.oracle.settle and I5), and a violation that names no window (W6 palette, W5 app-wide panel) marks none

layout.description: LayoutModel values per screen of each workspace a window shows (the focused one and the ones sidebar.multiView shows beside it): the split, strip, column and row tree with ratios, widths and heights at 3 dp, docks on their columns, zoom, focus, the strip's column count and the free canvas. Nothing the views report (frames, LayoutModel.visiblePanes, the strip's scroll offset) and nothing fitted to the viewport.

strip.description: the screen's scrolling column strip. Which columns show is not here: the scroll offset (ScreenContentView.scrollState) and the panes the view reports visible (LayoutModel.visiblePanes) are view state that changes with the window width and on every frame of a scroll.

columns.description: the columns that are not docked; a screen stored as one split tree is one implicit column (LayoutScreen.implicitColumnID)

canvas.description: the screen shown as a free canvas (LayoutModel.canvases), null when it is not one. Pane frames are not here: a canvas seeds them from the view's frames when it opens, so they depend on the window size.

zoom.description: the camera's zoom; null in the overview, whose camera is fitted to the viewport the view reports (CanvasCamera.fitting)

sidebar.description: The active window's sidebar: its rows in model order (each section, then its groups, a group before its subgroups and members, and loose workspaces; members of a collapsed group or section stay listed with the fold on the header).

window.description: the window whose sidebar this is

editing.description: the sidebar's edit mode (Edit Sidebar: items wiggle, Add Items and Done show)

selection.description: the multi-selection (Cmd/Shift-click) in tree order; holds the selected workspace

label.description: a workspace's title or a group's name (names a case sets); a section's kind (pinned, local, cloud, ssh, server) or a custom section's title; null for a document item, whose title can be a tab's

tabs.description: Per pane that lists a browser or page tab: the tab it shows and its browser and page tabs as its strip lists them (daemon tabs, then its window's session-local browser tabs, then internal page tabs, less the tabs the strip hides while they move to a dock or the side), read through the engine-neutral BrowserTab protocol (Chromium's TabRendererData analog). The find bar is overlays.findBar.

x-oracle-source.from: BrowserTab.state of the live page, else the daemon tab record

selected.description: the tab the pane shows, of any kind (a terminal too); null when no window remembers one

title.description: page text; null when the page has no title

page.description: the internal page a page tab shows (InternalPageID); null for a browser tab

engine.description: BrowserTab.engineKind of the live page, else the record's engine; null for a page tab

loadState.description: BrowserLoadPhase of the live page; unloaded when the tab has no engine page now (none made yet, or a hibernated or not-yet-started stand-in, as Chrome gives a discarded tab TabNetworkState::kNone); canGoBack, canGoForward, audible, crashed and unresponsive are then false

crashed.description: the page's content process ended (the sad tab)

unresponsive.description: the page's content process stopped answering input and the tab shows Page unresponsive (BrowserTabState.isUnresponsive; Chrome's hung renderer, WebContentsDelegate::RendererUnresponsive); false when the tab has no engine page or its process ended

hibernated.description: the page was discarded to free memory (DormantTabs; Chrome's is_tab_discarded)

overlays.description: Overlay stack, palette, dialog, hover card, find bar.

items.description: palette entry id (action or result id), stable across runs

target.description: hovered item id; normalize takes the kind whose x-oracle-id-patterns entry matches

settings.description: Hash of the applied effective config and its non-default keys.

motion.description: the motion arm, read back (task p15-oracle-233)

intents.description: Pending intents, monotonic outcome totals and the last refusal.

x-oracle-source.from: the daemon store's intent log and IntentTotals (store intents sent through daemon.intentEffect) and the refused perform turns OracleActionTurns counts

target.description: the public id of the one object the intent changes (ws_, screen_, pane_, tab_, grp_, tgrp_), relabeled by the x-oracle-id-patterns kind it matches; null when it changes no one public object (a column's rows, a close of several tabs) or the object has no public id yet

totals.description: process totals; the runner diffs two checkpoints

applied.description: intents that left the log on their echo or settle sequence

rolledBack.description: intents whose command failed: the store took their change back

refused.description: perform turns whose action did not run or whose handler refused

lastRefusal.description: what was refused last in this app process; I3 reads it from the raw checkpoint with a refused or rolledBack delta

x-oracle-volatile.reason: process-wide: it names the last refusal of whatever ran before in this app process, so it depends on the cases the session ran first; only the totals' deltas are per case

action.description: the canonical action id of the last refused perform turn, never the localized reason

intent.description: the case name of the last intent rolled back (renamePane), never its payload

windows.description: Window count, order, key and main, frames as screen fractions.

frame.description: window frame as fractions of its screen's visible frame (of the whole screen for a full-screen window), origin top left; a window on no screen fails the snapshot

title.description: a closed terminal tab's title is a shell title

agents.description: Each agent chat tab's acpmux session (the store's tab record, acpmux's lane from the app's watch) and the conversation each Home Messages view shows. Hashes only: no prompt, reply, title or draft text.

x-oracle-source.from: agent chat tab records, the acpmux lane mirror, the unsent-draft store and the Home pages (hashes only)

sessions.description: one row per agent chat tab, a new chat with no session yet too

session.description: the tab record's acpmux session; null for a new chat before its first prompt

agent.description: the harness the tab records (claude, codex, ...), else the lane's; null while unknown

state.description: acpmux's lane state for the session; unknown with no lane (no session, the watch down, another machine's chat)

turn.description: acpmux's turnCount for the session; 0 with no lane

pendingApprovals.description: acpmux's pendingPermissions for the session; 0 with no lane

draftSha256.description: sha256 of the composer text the app keeps for a new chat (AgentUnsentDrafts); null when none. A started chat's draft is acpmux's and the page's (webviews facet)

home.description: each Home Messages view: a window's Home top page, a Home tab, the docked Home

window.description: the window whose Home top page this is; null for a tab

tab.description: the Home tab or docked Home tab; null for a top page

conversation.description: the conversation the view shows (selected in its list); null on New Message, on a docked Home that shows Channels, or before one shows

terminals.description: Terminal attach state, size, title, cwd and a hash of the last 24 lines.

x-oracle-source.derive: sha256 of the last 24 rows of /text split on newline, after the path rewrite

webviews.description: Per-page store summary from each app web page.

page.description: page kind (route id such as settings or app-store), a fixed name and not an instance id; tab and pane identify the instance

ax.description: Accessibility tree of focusable and actionable elements.

x-oracle-source.from: AX tree of focusable and actionable elements

labelKey.description: localization key, never the shown text; "<ambiguous>" when the shown text is that of several keys and the element names none; null when it is no app string

crashes.description: Child-process exits by kind: totals since the app launched (holder: since the daemon owner started; a new owner counts from 0, which I17 reads as a reset). renderer counts each renderer process once, not each tab it hosted. daemon counts the owner ends the app's connection saw without daemon-shutdown (a crash or a kill, not a requested stop). The runner and I17 take the rise between checkpoints.

x-oracle-source.from: CEFChildProcessMonitor's helper exits (BrowserCrashLog tallies), CrashRecoveryService's previous run, the daemon connection's drops without daemon-shutdown, and the daemon's oracle-state childExits (holders its owner counted ending)

exits.description: the exits the app saw, oldest first; I17 reads the entries past the previous checkpoint's from the raw checkpoint

x-oracle-volatile.reason: process-wide: it lists every exit since the app launched, so it depends on the cases the session ran first; only the counts' rises are per case
checks run per frame; the count follows the host frame rate

switches.description: Refactor switch arms read back and per-site hits.

arms.description: switch name to the arm read back from the frozen value

x-oracle-volatile.reason: per-frame reads scale with the host frame rate

cli.description: The receipt of a cli step (invariant I1), in that step's settled checkpoint: the exit code of its `cmux` call, its stdout and the typed code of a failed call. stdout is open: one JSON value, JSON lines as an array, or the text, with the rules of open objects (ids by x-oracle-id-patterns, x-oracle-open-keys, the path and url rewrites).

x-oracle-source.from: the shipped cmux binary run by driver_cli.py (VM: the run SHA's cmux-tui; fleet: CMUX_TAG=<tag> scripts/cmux-debug-cli.sh)

error.description: the code of the JSON error a failed call writes to stderr (`--json`), else cli.failed; present only when exit is not 0

mcp.description: The receipt of an mcp step (invariant I1), in that step's settled checkpoint: whether the tools/call result is a tool error, the result's structuredContent (its content when it has none), and the typed code of a failed call. result is open, with the rules of open objects (ids by x-oracle-id-patterns, x-oracle-open-keys, the path and url rewrites).

x-oracle-source.from: `cmux mcp serve --all-tools` over stdio, run by driver_mcp.py (VM: the run SHA's cmux-tui; fleet: the tagged bundle's cmux on the app's socket)

error.description: the code of the tool error's envelope (structuredContent.error.code), or mcp.rpc_error for a JSON-RPC error; present only when isError is true

reply.description: The reply of a resource.call step whose expect outcome is any (a walk move of scripts/cmux-next/oracle/gen_walks.py), in that step's settled checkpoint: ok with the mutation receipt's replayed flag, or the typed error code. The daemon facet beside it holds the state the call left; the reply's value is left out because the facet shows its objects.

x-oracle-source.from: the step's reply on the daemon driver's ProtocolConnection (driver_daemon.py)

replayed.description: an ok mutation_result's replayed flag: true when the daemon answered from the idempotency record of an earlier call with the same key (I10)

error.description: the typed error code; present only when outcome is error

tui.description: The cmux-tui frontend of a case that requires tui, attached on a PTY the driver owns: its last complete frame after the settle probe (or, at a turn checkpoint, the first frame that met the step's waitFor). The grid size, the sha256 of the frame's row text and style runs (screenSha256: the case's session name and state root written as the fixture's; a change of color alone changes it, and private text is never recorded), the cursor, and the frontend's exit code once it has exited.

x-oracle-source.from: the PTY output of `cmux-tui attach`, kept as a character grid by driver_tui.py (VM: the run SHA's cmux-tui)

screenSha256.description: sha256 (UTF-8) of the row text, a blank line, then the style runs: the rows' text with trailing blanks dropped and the case's names renamed, joined by newlines; then each row's runs of one canonical SGR style, `count*style` joined by `|` (style: the sorted attribute names and colors, `bold,fg=5:110`; empty for the default), rows joined by newlines

cursor.description: the cursor; a hidden cursor has no position (it stays where the last drawn cell was)

exit.description: the frontend's exit code once it has exited (a detach), null while it runs

notComparable.description: The build has no source for this facet (v0 base, failed overlay, unsupported product).

layoutNode.description: one LayoutModel node. split: a binary split (SplitNode), ratios [a, b]; strip: a screen's columns in model order; column: one LayoutColumn, its rows or its one tree as children, with width and dock; row: one LayoutRow, its tree as the one child, with height; leaf: a pane. stack is the daemon's, which LayoutMapping shows as a leaf.

oneOf.description: a column: its width and its dock, no height
a row: its height, no width or dock
a split, strip, stack or leaf: no width, height or dock

ratios.description: a split's child shares, sum 1; empty on other kinds

width.description: a column's width as a fraction of the viewport

height.description: a row's height as a fraction of the column's viewport height

dock.description: the edge a column is pinned to, null for a scrolling column
